rule.title: Discriminated Unions for Representing State
rule.statement: Asynchronous UI states must be modeled using Discriminated Unions with a common literal discriminator property ('status') to make impossible states unrepresentable.
rule.rationale: Using independent booleans (isLoading: boolean, isError: boolean, data: T | null) allows contradictory states like { isLoading: true, isError: true }.
rule.implementation_guidance: type State = { status: 'idle' } | { status: 'loading' } | { status: 'success'; data: T } | { status: 'error'; error: string };

forbidden.example: if (isLoading && !isError && data) ... // Error-prone boolean permutation checks

preferred.example: switch (state.status) { case 'loading': return <Skeleton />; case 'success': return <View data={state.data} />; }

source.section: Item 28: Prefer Types That Always Represent Valid States
source.evidence_quote: Types that represent valid states make your code easier to write and reduce bugs. Discriminated unions make impossible states unrepresentable.
